# D8_TRIGDEBUG_B6f77f23d: tm45 bars + trig_levels_opens false_break_native (M 3, k 0.5), bracket asym15u/30u, both sides, NY AM session of trading date 20261110 plus the 300 bars before it (W-D8SPEC, relay order 0400Z)

Documentation only. Series: ONE continuous series of all 45-second epoch bars (`tm45`, 1,702,955 bars, all sessions, 2023-04 to 2026-11-13; stored engine bars = the BASE set: time bars are unaffected by the print rule). Rows below: bar index 1696534 to 1697033; the NY AM bars of 20261110 are sess 3 and td 20261110 (idx 1696834 to 1697033, 200 bars; 19 events). I recomputed T0, the seven lines at T0, u, the event, the fired line and the bracket with the engine's own helpers and checked that my signals over the whole series equal the module's `signal_fn` (58,993 signals; equal = True). The stop/target of the 19 events equal the engine events file `_nye/ev/B6f77f23d.parquet` (all 120/120 points on this day because the bracket unit clips; the file has 19 NY AM events on this date).

## 1. The bar: tm45 (code `th_swap/tbars.py time_bars`; rule text D8_BAR_DEFS.md section 8)
- Bucket k = floor(print time in ns / 45e9): **boundaries are multiples of 45 s since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC** (a pattern :00, :45, :30, :15 repeating every 3 minutes; because 3600 / 45 = 80 it coincides with NT8's session-anchored 45-second bars on every day). A print exactly ON a boundary belongs to the NEW bar. Empty buckets give no bar.
- **Known time = max(nominal bucket end, timestamp of the first print of the next existing bucket)**: the bar closes when the first tick of the next bar arrives (milliseconds after the boundary in the NY session). No session reset (continuous series, roll ignored); a bar is labelled with the session of its NOMINAL END time (a bar ending at 09:30:00 ET is NY AM).
- O/H/L/C from the prints of the bucket, volume = contracts.

## 2. The lines (code: `triggers_d/lv_opens.py`, `fd_levels.py`, `fd_common.py`): which opens are levels
All lines are PRICES (raw domain) read from the 1-minute grid; each is the OPEN price of one 1-minute bar (the first trade price of that minute) and is NaN before the minute that makes it known:
- **T_P0930** = open of the 09:30 ET minute of the trading date (first trade price of RTH), valid from the 09:31 minute on (value 27743.0 from 2026-11-10T14:30:00.000000000Z). **T_P1000** = open of the 10:00 ET minute, valid from 10:01 (28011.75, 2026-11-10T15:00:00.000000000Z).
- **OPEN_DAY** = open of the 18:00 ET minute of the Globex day (first minute of the trading date; 28064.0 at 2026-11-09T23:00:00.000000000Z), valid from 18:01. **OPEN_0000** = open of the 00:00 ET minute (27969.5 at 2026-11-10T05:00:00.000000000Z), valid from 00:01. **OPEN_0200** = open of the 02:00 ET minute (27985.0 at 2026-11-10T07:00:00.000000000Z), valid from 02:01.
- **OPEN_WEEK** = open of the first minute of the ISO week of the trading date (week starts Sunday 18:00 ET; 26878.5 at 2026-11-08T23:00:00.000000000Z), **OPEN_MONTH** = open of the first minute of the calendar month of the trading date: **in the engine's data this is 26974.25 at 2026-11-05T16:00:00.000000000Z, because the November tape hole (11-02 to 11-04 and the morning of 11-05 missing) makes 2026-11-05 16:00 UTC the first minute of the month; the true November open differs, so OPEN_MONTH in NT8 will not equal the engine's for November.** Both weekly and monthly lines are shifted by one minute (known once the minute has opened).
- Minute opens use the same 1-minute bars as the VWAP lines (first trade of each UTC minute; D8_TRIGDEBUG_L7cc56d99.md). A line is NaN when its minute is missing or older than 120 s at T0.

## 3. The trigger (code `lv_base.make`, `fd_common.level_events`, variant false_break_native)
- **T0** of bar j = floor to whole seconds of the KNOWN time of bar j-1 (no open time in the series); the lines are read at the last minute start <= T0 within 120 s.
- **u (native)** = trailing median of the bar range (high - low) of the previous 100 bars (current bar excluded, >= 20 bars), floor 0.5 points; **k x u = 0.5 u**.
- **Per line:** up(j) = close[j] > line + 0.5 u, dn(j) = close[j] < line - 0.5 u. **SHORT** (failed upside break) when up was true on ANY of the 3 previous bars (j-3..j-1) AND close[j] < line (edge: the first bar where this becomes true); **LONG** (failed downside break) when dn was true on any of the 3 previous bars AND close[j] > line. A bar with both a long and a short on different lines is dropped; the fired line is the first with an event in the order T_P0930, T_P1000, OPEN_DAY, OPEN_0000, OPEN_0200, OPEN_WEEK, OPEN_MONTH. Event time = floor(known time to whole seconds) + 2 s.
- **Bracket asym15u/30u** (code `gjob.bracket_arrays`, `ny_build.events`): u50 = trailing 50-bar median of the bar range (high - low) INCLUDING the signal bar, at least 10 bars (NaN replaced by the series median, floor 0.25 pt) - a different unit from the native u above. **Stop = 15 x u50 points, target = 30 x u50 points, each clipped to [10, 120] points**; measured from the entry fill. Exit = end of the session of the signal (12:00 ET = 17:00 UTC for NY AM) with the 120 s no-print exit cap. Columns below.

## 5. History NT8 must load (plain paragraph)
The five intraday/daily opens (T_P0930, T_P1000, OPEN_DAY, OPEN_0000, OPEN_0200) need only the current trading date's 1-minute opens (OPEN_DAY from 18:00 ET), so a chart started the previous evening is enough. OPEN_WEEK needs the minutes since Sunday 18:00 ET of the trading week (up to 6 calendar days) and OPEN_MONTH the first minute of the calendar month (up to 31 days; note the engine artefact above for November 2026). The unit u needs the 100 previous 45-second bars (about 75 minutes) and u50 the 50 previous (about 38 minutes) of the continuous series, which cross session boundaries, so tick processing should start at least 3 hours before the first bar tested. The bars themselves are epoch-aligned 45 s buckets built from every tick with the next-print close rule; they do not depend on the print-merge rule. Nothing else (no book, no other instrument) is used.
